As already said a very focused deck, so I will offer just a few (and maybe
marginal suggestions):

> Potence-Celerity Seek and Destroy
>
> Crypt: (12 cards)
> 1 Anvil
> 1 Amalia
> 3 Beast, LfoD
> 1 Caspare Giovanni
> 1 Dre, LotCD
> 1 Jacob Bragg
> 2 Jimmy Dunn
> 1 Richter
> 1 Sela
>

You have a reasonable amount of rush in the deck, so 3 Beast seem a bit
excessive (and risky), because you want to hit hard and fast, and you need
many minions to do that. Together with Amelia and Richter you have 5
7-caps... Too many. How about Victor Tolliver and maybe also Volker? The deck
is not strictly POT/cel, it has many good Celerity cards, and you might find
room to up the number of Potence Masters (take out one Dreams maybe).

> Library: (85 cards)
> Master (13)
> 2 Blood doll
> 3 Dreams of the Sphinx
> 4 Haven Uncovered
> 2 Minion Tap
> 2 Potence
>

Minion Tap is okayish for the big guys, but I think Blood Dolls are generally
better in this sort of deck.

> Minion (72 cards)
> 7 Blur
> 7 Bums Rush
> 4 Decapitate
> 6 Disarm
> 2 Fists of Death
> 8 Flash
> 10 Immortal Grapple
> 3 Pushing the Limit
> 2 Rampage
> 7 Taste of Vitae
> 9 Torn Signpost
> 7 Undead Strenght
>

Do you see many maneuvers and second round combat in your playgroup? 8 Flash
seem a lot to me, maybe some Pursuit (maneuver, add. strike at superior)
might go in instead - or some extra rush if you take my advice and cut down
the number of Beasts.

Regards

Hmm, this deck should eat all Tremere for lunch. Guns and Assamites, though,
might pose a problem. Still I think dual-use cards like Pursuit would be good
to avoid handjam if you are not trying to catch Assamites - which might be a
serious problem anyway, 'cause even with 8 Flash you will have a hard time
keeping up if they rush you. Best bet would be a well-timed Bum's Rush as
soon as one of the Silent Killers hits the table. Or just tell that new
player that Malkavian stealth bleed is the way to go ;-) About Tory Artillery
decks I wouldn’t worry too much - you have enough time to eliminate any
threat by pre-emptively killing the vampire before she equips.

Fame won't help you too much honestly. Don't be afraid of the hard labour it
takes to oust by bleeding one pool at a time. If the deck goes alright you
will have a very stable position, and you should be able to afford the time.
Include 1 Fame as a prayer card - it might help, for sure, but this card is
not the ultimate solution to the problem (See the thread on Fame as a pure
stratgey for ousting a while back). Try and work the table, you can always
sell a cross-table rush for a nicely spread Conservative Agitation by your
grandprey's political deck.

Messages.Body:
Tim Eijpe wrote:
>
> Now this is a first. Normally I would play a weenie Potence deck or a
> Weenie Pot-Obf deck, however those got old really fast. So it was time

> 1 Anvil
> 1 Amalia
> 3 Beast, LfoD
> 1 Caspare Giovanni
> 1 Dre, LotCD
> 1 Jacob Bragg
> 2 Jimmy Dunn
> 1 Richter
> 1 Sela

I would put in a couple Potence-only guys, since your celerity angle
seems to be only Blur and Flash. You can still have a pretty successful
combat without these cards. Maybe lose a Richter and a Beast for two of
Lupo/KoKo/Hugo.

> Library: (85 cards)
> Master (13)
> 2 Blood doll
> 3 Dreams of the Sphinx
> 4 Haven Uncovered
> 2 Minion Tap
> 2 Potence

Since currently your crypt only has two people with pot instead of POT,
I would remove both Potence masters. More Blood Dolls; every Taste
gains you pool. I prefer the Dolls to the Taps. You're better off
having smaller vampires (which you won't need to tap, and which will
come out faster).

> Minion (72 cards)
> 7 Blur
> 7 Bums Rush

This (plus 2 Rampages) is 13 rush cards. You might want a few more.

> 4 Decapitate
> 6 Disarm
> 2 Fists of Death
> 8 Flash
> 10 Immortal Grapple
> 3 Pushing the Limit

How about more Fists of Death instead of these? That works better with
Blur.

> 2 Rampage
> 7 Taste of Vitae
> 9 Torn Signpost
> 7 Undead Strenght

Otherwise, this looks pretty standard. You might want to look through
the deck archives for decks by Josh Duffin and myself to compare.

James

Yes.

The acting vampire's action was blocked (card text on Obedience),
and Millicent says that that results in Millicent and the acting
vampire being burned.

Yes, by the same reasoning.

Messages.Author: Tom Kassel
Messages.Body:
In article <943jes$be8$1...@nnrp1.deja.com>,
Tim Eijpe <t_e...@my-deja.com> wrote:

> Exactly, the only thing against Obedience is that you'll have to enter
> combat. With sufficient stealth no combat occurs. However, any Rush
deck
> will fail in sight of Obedience IMO.

That doesn't seem a foregone conclusion. Passive defence like
Obedience leaves the attacker unscathed, ready for another go. Quite
different from the treatment the Gangrel or Tzimisce might deal. The
only thing that the rusher loses is time - important I'll concede but
less bad than loss of time and minion.

When the target is known or expected to use Obedience, you must expect
that it will take several attempts to get into combat with the desired
minion. If you happen to find your hand jammed with Bum's Rush/Ambush,
this is a fine opportunity to loosen things up. Otherwise, Haven
Uncovered is the weapon of choice, giving you a combat opportunity for
each of your minions. At the worst, the target minion has to waste his
next action removing the haven or face another multiple onslaught.

Tom
